evals.prompt: /cyoda:setup — I want cyoda running locally on my laptop.
evals.expected_output: Runs cyoda-status.sh (STATUS=unreachable for the implicit default http://localhost:8080, with WARN lines 'no saved profile; using the default local instance http://localhost:8080 — type /cyoda:setup to save it' and 'no cyoda-go is answering at http://localhost:8080 — type /cyoda:setup to install or start one'), goes to local mode without offering to switch profiles, finds no cyoda binary, runs `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda` (succeeds), runs `cyoda init`, starts `cyoda`, polls http://localhost:8080/api/health until {"status":"UP"}, writes the `default` profile {endpoint: http://localhost:8080, env: development} as active with no token or tokenCommand, re-runs cyoda-status.sh and reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [profile: default]', says mock auth needs no token, and ends with 'next, type `/cyoda:build`'.

files._simulated/machine.md: No `cyoda` on PATH. Homebrew is installed and `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda` succeeds; afterwards `cyoda --version` prints `cyoda version 0.8.4 (commit e861154)`. `cyoda init` succeeds. No config file at ~/.config/cyoda/cyoda-plugin-config.json. Port 8080 is free; once `cyoda` is started, GET http://localhost:8080/api/health returns {"status":"UP"} and GET /api/help returns {"version":"0.8.4",...}.

assertions.text: Runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/cyoda-status.sh` before installing anything
Installs with exactly `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda` (no `brew tap cyoda-platform/...`, no other formula name)
Runs `cyoda init` and then starts the server with `cyoda`
Verifies readiness with GET http://localhost:8080/api/health (expects {"status":"UP"}); does not probe /readyz on the API port
Writes ~/.config/cyoda/cyoda-plugin-config.json with active `default` and profile `default` containing only endpoint http://localhost:8080 and env development (no token, no tokenCommand)
Reports the result in the form 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [profile: default]'
Says the local instance runs mock auth, so no token or /cyoda:auth is needed
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud or offer a cloud option
The hand-off says 'next, type `/cyoda:build`' (or another `/cyoda:<x>`) with a one-line reason and does not say it will invoke or run another skill itself

evals.expected_output: Finds no cyoda binary, tries `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda`, which fails with a permission error. Does not diagnose Homebrew, does not run brew doctor or sudo. Shows the verbatim 'run it yourself' message including the install list (brew, the install.sh curl line, the release page, the Docker image ghcr.io/cyoda/cyoda) and waits for the developer before continuing with `cyoda init`.

files._simulated/machine.md: No `cyoda` on PATH. `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda` exits 1 with: `Error: Permission denied @ dir_s_mkdir - /opt/homebrew/Cellar`. No config file at ~/.config/cyoda/cyoda-plugin-config.json.

assertions.text: Shows the message starting 'I couldn't complete the installation — this usually needs to run in your own terminal.' with `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda`, copied verbatim from the skill

The message lists all four routes: brew, `curl -fsSL https://github.com/cyoda/cyoda-go/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`, the GitHub release page https://github.com/cyoda/cyoda-go/releases, and the Docker image `ghcr.io/cyoda/cyoda`
Does not run `brew doctor`, `sudo`, chmod/chown, or any other Homebrew fix, and adds no extra advice to the message
Stops and waits for the developer to confirm the install before running `cyoda init`
Does not mention `cyoda-platform/cyoda-go` or `brew tap`
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud

evals.prompt: /cyoda:setup — connect to our team's dev instance at https://cyoda-dev.internal.example.com/api/
evals.expected_output: Uses connect mode. Normalises the endpoint to https://cyoda-dev.internal.example.com (drops the trailing /api/), probes /api/health (UP), asks development or production (developer says development), asks for a profile name other than `default` (developer says team-dev), writes {endpoint, env} to profile team-dev and makes it active, probes GET /api/model/ without a token and gets 401, so it says the instance needs a token and ends with 'next, type `/cyoda:auth`'.

files._simulated/instance.md: GET https://cyoda-dev.internal.example.com/api/health returns {"status":"UP"}. GET /api/help returns {"version":"0.8.4",...}. GET /api/model/ without an Authorization header returns 401. The developer answers: env development; profile name team-dev.

assertions.text: Stores the endpoint as https://cyoda-dev.internal.example.com (no trailing /api or slash)
Probes <endpoint>/api/health before writing the profile
Asks whether the instance is development or production
Writes profile team-dev with only endpoint and env (no token, no secret, no tokenCommand yet), keeps the existing `default` profile, and sets active to team-dev
Detects that the instance is not mock auth from the 401 on an unauthenticated GET /api/model/
Does not ask for a client id, secret or token
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
Hands off with 'next, type `/cyoda:auth`' and a one-line reason; does not say it will invoke the auth skill

evals.expected_output: cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=unreachable for the active profile `old`, with WARN lines 'profile old contains a stored token, which this plugin no longer reads; you can remove it' and 'active profile old is unreachable; run /cyoda:setup to switch to default'. The skill shows both warnings as they are, offers to switch the active profile to `default`, and on yes sets active to default (local cyoda is already installed and healthy), leaving the old profile in place, and reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [profile: default]'.

files._simulated/instance.md: `cyoda --version` prints `cyoda version 0.8.4`. https://gone.example.com does not answer. http://localhost:8080/api/health returns {"status":"UP"}. The developer answers yes to switching to default.

assertions.text: Shows the warning 'profile old contains a stored token, which this plugin no longer reads; you can remove it' in neutral wording
Offers to switch the active profile to `default` because `old` is unreachable
Does not read, print, or use the stored token value
Does not delete the old profile or its token field without the developer's yes
Does not reinstall cyoda, since `cyoda --version` already reports 0.8.4
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud or suggest that the old endpoint was a cloud instance

evals.prompt: /cyoda:setup — link this project to its cyoda-go. It runs in our Docker Compose stack.
evals.expected_output: Runs cyoda-status.sh first. The working directory is the git repo `shop` (not $HOME), so it offers to link this project. It proposes the git top level /Users/dev/work/shop as the project root and the developer confirms; the key is its real path (`pwd -P`). Docker is on PATH, so it runs ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/cyoda-docker-instances.sh (read-only) and lists shop-cyoda-1 (compose shop, http://localhost:8082) and billing-cyoda-1 (compose billing, http://localhost:8080). The developer picks shop. It probes http://localhost:8082/api/health (UP) and the version 0.8.4 from /api/help, asks development or production (development), probes GET /api/model/ without a token (401), asks how tokens are obtained (the project's `scripts/auth.sh token`), test-runs that from the project root with CYODA_ENDPOINT set without printing the token (3 parts), then writes projects["/Users/dev/work/shop"] = {endpoint: http://localhost:8082, env: development, tokenCommand: "scripts/auth.sh token"} into the plugin config with jq to a temp file and mv, mode 0600, keeping the default profile and active. Nothing is written into the project tree. Finishes with cyoda-status.sh: 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8082 [project: shop]'.

files._simulated/instance.md:
The working directory is the root of the git repo `shop`; `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `pwd -P` both print /Users/dev/work/shop (not $HOME). There is no .cyoda/ dir. cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=connected PROFILE=default ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=profile` (the billing stack's instance). `command -v docker` succeeds. `cyoda-docker-instances.sh` prints:
```
CONTAINER=shop-cyoda-1 COMPOSE_PROJECT=shop ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8082 IMAGE=ghcr.io/cyoda/cyoda:0.8.4
CONTAINER=billing-cyoda-1 COMPOSE_PROJECT=billing ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 IMAGE=ghcr.io/cyoda/cyoda:0.8.4
```
GET http://localhost:8082/api/health returns {"status":"UP"}; GET /api/help returns {"version":"0.8.4",...}; GET /api/model/ without an Authorization header returns 401. Running `scripts/auth.sh token` from the project root with CYODA_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8082 prints a 3-part JWT (exit 0). After the write, cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=connected PROFILE=shop ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8082 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop`. The developer answers: yes, that root; the shop one; development; tokens come from `scripts/auth.sh token`.

assertions.text: Recognises it is inside a project directory (a git repo, not $HOME) and goes to linking this project, rather than local install or a machine-wide connect profile
Proposes the git top level /Users/dev/work/shop as the project root and lets the developer confirm or change it

Lists the running cyoda-go containers with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/cyoda-docker-instances.sh and shows both with compose project and endpoint (shop → http://localhost:8082, billing → http://localhost:8080), letting the developer pick or type a URL
Runs no docker command that changes anything: no docker run/start/stop/restart/rm, no docker compose up/down
Probes http://localhost:8082/api/health (UP) and reads the version from /api/help before writing anything
Asks whether the instance is development or production

Detects that a token is needed from the 401 on an unauthenticated GET /api/model/, asks how tokens are obtained, keeps the relative command `scripts/auth.sh token`, and test-runs it from the project root without printing the token

Writes the binding as `projects["/Users/dev/work/shop"]` (the real path from `pwd -P`) in the plugin config ${CYODA_PLUGIN_CONFIG:-~/.config/cyoda/cyoda-plugin-config.json}, with exactly endpoint http://localhost:8082, env development and tokenCommand `scripts/auth.sh token`, via jq to a temp file then mv, mode 0600; no token, client id or secret in it
Keeps the `default` profile and `active` unchanged in the plugin config
Writes nothing into the project tree: no .cyoda/ file, no .gitignore change
Finishes by re-running cyoda-status.sh and reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8082 [project: shop]'
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud

evals.expected_output: cyoda-status.sh, run in the linked project `shop`, prints STATUS=unreachable PROFILE=shop ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8082 … SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop and WARN=project shop is bound to http://localhost:8082, which is unreachable; start that instance, or type /cyoda:setup to link this project to another one. The skill shows the warning. It does NOT offer to switch the machine-wide active profile to `default` and does not edit the plugin config. It offers to start the project's stack, given as a command for the developer to run in their own terminal (the project has a compose.yaml, so e.g. `docker compose up -d` in the project dir), then re-run cyoda-status.sh; or to re-link the project. The developer starts the stack and says so; the re-check shows STATUS=connected and the skill reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8082 [project: shop]'. It runs no state-changing docker command itself.

files._simulated/instance.md: The working directory is /Users/dev/work/shop, the root of the git repo `shop`. First cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=unreachable PROFILE=shop ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8082 ENV=development VERSION=none BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop` and `WARN=project shop is bound to http://localhost:8082, which is unreachable; start that instance, or type /cyoda:setup to link this project to another one`. The shop Compose stack is stopped. The developer answers: they'll start the stack, and later say "it's up". After that, cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=connected PROFILE=shop ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8082 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop`.

assertions.text: Shows the 'project shop is bound to http://localhost:8082, which is unreachable; …' warning as the script printed it
Does not offer or perform a switch of the machine-wide active profile to `default`, and does not write to the plugin config
Offers to start the project's stack as a command for the developer to run (e.g. `docker compose up -d` in the project dir) or to re-link the project
Does not itself run docker compose up, docker start or any other docker command that changes state
After the developer says the stack is up, re-runs cyoda-status.sh and reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8082 [project: shop]'
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud

evals.prompt: /cyoda:setup — re-link this project, we moved the shop stack to port 8086.
evals.expected_output: cyoda-status.sh prints SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop (connected to http://localhost:8082). The developer wants to re-link, so it goes to link mode with the existing entry's key `/Users/dev/work/shop` (from PROJECT) as the root. It takes http://localhost:8086 (typed URL), probes /api/health (UP) and /api/help (0.8.4), asks the env (development), probes GET /api/model/ without a token (401) and keeps the existing tokenCommand `scripts/auth.sh token` after the developer confirms (test-run from the project root, 3 parts). It replaces projects["/Users/dev/work/shop"] (jq to a temp file, mv, 0600), so the map still has exactly one entry for this project, then reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8086 [project: shop]'.

files._simulated/instance.md: The working directory is /Users/dev/work/shop (git top level and `pwd -P`). First cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=connected PROFILE=shop ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8082 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop`. `command -v docker` fails (no docker). GET http://localhost:8086/api/health returns {"status":"UP"}; GET /api/help returns {"version":"0.8.4",...}; GET /api/model/ without a token returns 401. `scripts/auth.sh token` from the project root with CYODA_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8086 prints a 3-part JWT. After the write, cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=connected PROFILE=shop ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8086 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop`. The developer answers: yes, re-link this root; http://localhost:8086; development; keep scripts/auth.sh token.

assertions.text: Uses the existing entry's key /Users/dev/work/shop (the status PROJECT value) as the key to replace
Probes http://localhost:8086/api/health and /api/help before writing

Replaces projects["/Users/dev/work/shop"] with endpoint http://localhost:8086 (env development, tokenCommand scripts/auth.sh token) atomically with mode 0600, leaving exactly one entry for this project and the profiles unchanged
Reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8086 [project: shop]'
Writes nothing into the project tree: no .cyoda/ file, no .gitignore change
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud

evals.prompt: /cyoda:setup — unlink this project, I want it to use my normal profile again.
evals.expected_output: cyoda-status.sh prints SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop. It confirms the unlink, deletes projects["/Users/dev/work/shop"] (the PROJECT key) from the plugin config with jq to a temp file and mv, mode 0600, keeping profiles and active, then re-runs cyoda-status.sh, which now shows SOURCE=profile, and reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [profile: default]'.

files._simulated/instance.md: The working directory is /Users/dev/work/shop. First cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=connected PROFILE=shop ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8082 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop`. After the entry is removed, cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=connected PROFILE=default ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=profile`. assertions.text: Deletes projects["/Users/dev/work/shop"] (the key from status PROJECT) from the plugin config via jq to a temp file then mv, mode 0600, keeping `profiles` and `active`
Asks for confirmation before deleting the entry
Re-runs cyoda-status.sh and reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [profile: default]'
Writes nothing into the project tree: no .cyoda/ file, no .gitignore change

evals.expected_output: Link mode in /Users/dev/work/sioms. The project has a legacy `.cyoda/config` written by an older plugin with endpoint http://localhost:8080, env development and a `token` field. The skill reads only its endpoint and env (e.g. `jq '{endpoint, env}'`), never shows or copies the token, and offers once to import them; the developer agrees. It probes http://localhost:8080/api/health (UP) and /api/help (0.8.4), confirms env development, probes GET /api/model/ without a token (200: mock auth, no tokenCommand), and writes projects["/Users/dev/work/sioms"] = {endpoint: http://localhost:8080, env: development} into the plugin config atomically, mode 0600. It then says the old file is no longer read and gives `rm .cyoda/config` (or `rm -r .cyoda`) for the developer to run, without deleting it itself. Reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [project: sioms]'.

files._simulated/instance.md: The working directory is /Users/dev/work/sioms, the git top level (`pwd -P` prints the same). cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=connected PROFILE=team ENDPOINT=https://cyoda-dev.example.com ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=profile`. `command -v docker` fails. GET http://localhost:8080/api/health returns {"status":"UP"}; GET /api/help returns {"version":"0.8.4",...}; GET /api/model/ without a token returns 200. After the write, cyoda-status.sh prints `STATUS=connected PROFILE=sioms ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/sioms`. The developer answers: yes, that root; yes, import; development.

assertions.text: Notices the legacy .cyoda/config and offers to import its endpoint and env into the project entry, asking the developer to confirm
Never prints, copies or stores the `token` from the legacy file (reads only endpoint and env) and stores no tokenCommand from it
Probes http://localhost:8080/api/health and /api/help before writing, and detects mock auth from a 200 on an unauthenticated GET /api/model/
Writes projects["/Users/dev/work/sioms"] = {endpoint: http://localhost:8080, env: development} into the plugin config atomically, mode 0600, keeping the `team` profile and `active`
Says the old .cyoda/config is no longer read and gives a command for the developer to delete it, without deleting it itself
Reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [project: sioms]'
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
